title: The Mathematics of Weight-Space Programming: Behavioral Geometry, Constructive Synthesis, and Proof-Carrying Neural Edits

target_networks.name: abstract parameter manifolds; two-layer ReLU networks for finite contracts
Qwen3 (archived earlier author study, model size not stated)

headline_result.text: A mathematical framework for weight edits (four-subspace decomposition, minimum-norm edits, exact finite ReLU compiler of width at most n-1); the only model evidence is an earlier Qwen3 study where 1,824 next-token forecasts matched but the continuous rank-one edit got 0 of 96 complete arithmetic answers versus 47 for baseline.
headline_result.quote: among 96 arithmetic prompts, the baseline obtained 47 complete answers, a selected 128-weight deletion obtained 50, and the continuous rank-one intervention obtained zero.

key_claims.claim: The paper frames WSP as an inverse problem: when an admissible weight edit exists for a desired behavior change under audit and retention constraints, its least cost, and how to certify it.
key_claims.quote: given a desired behavioral displacement, a collection of audit and retention constraints, and a metric on parameter space, when does an admissible weight program exist, what is its least cost, and how can its effect be certified?

key_claims.claim: A terminating exact-rational procedure compiles any consistent finite rational input-output contract into a two-layer ReLU network with at most n-1 hidden units.
key_claims.quote: A constructive result supplies a terminating exact-rational procedure that realizes every consistent finite rational input-output contract with a two-layer ReLU network of at most 𝑛 − 1 hidden units for 𝑛 ≥ 2.

key_claims.claim: The claim that every fixed architecture can realize every target behavior by a weight write is false.
key_claims.quote: Consequently the assertion that every fixed neural architecture can realize every possible target behavior by a parameter write is false.

key_claims.claim: Finite test observations cannot certify universal competence without a hypothesis class or regularity assumptions.
key_claims.quote: Therefore observations restricted to 𝑆 cannot establish equality of two unconstrained functions on all of 𝑋.

key_claims.claim: In the archived Qwen3 study, token-level forecasts were accurate but the full-response acceptance contract was not met.
key_claims.quote: The full acceptance contract was not met by the tested interventions.

limitations_stated.text: The global theorem does not prove bracket-generation or capability acquisition for any given transformer.
limitations_stated.quote: Not proved: bracket-generation for a given transformer, completeness of its horizontal paths, uniform global costs, or global acquisition of an unspecified capability.

limitations_stated.text: The finite compiler protects only enumerated samples, not a pretrained model's behavior on all inputs.
limitations_stated.quote: The construction protects only explicitly enumerated samples in its contract.

limitations_stated.text: Lean kernel verification of the main theorem is outstanding.
limitations_stated.quote: Lean-kernel acceptance for the complete eight-clause theorem is a distinct milestone and is recorded separately from the textual proofs and executable fixtures.

notes_for_review: A theory monograph (v3.3) that restates standard linear algebra, differential geometry and control results in the language of constrained weight edits; most theorems are textbook reductions applied under stated hypotheses, and the paper is explicit about what is not proved. No LLM acts as editor and no new experiments are run; the only model evidence is transcribed from an earlier unpublished Qwen3 study in which local token forecasts were exact but the rank-one edit destroyed complete-response arithmetic. Useful for the review as a formal statement that local predictability is not capability. The PDF is dated 19 November 2026 while the Zenodo manifest date is 2026-11-13.
